opening.argument: The presentation solicits paid participation in mining pools, including an offer to register after purchasing a $1,000 or $2,000 pool, while the speaker reports investing $1,500 in one pool. It presents mining results and projected Bitcoin earnings alongside pool-account figures, describing recovery of the investment in roughly 75 to 80 days and continued gains. Those financial expectations are speaker-reported, not verified outcomes, yet they are used to promote the purchase. The presentation also links profits to team development, displays commissions attributed to multiple team levels, and asks viewers to provide personal contact information. Taken together, the paid pool offer, projected returns, team-based income claims, and recruitment request establish the promotional pattern at issue without proving that any particular viewer suffered a loss.
